bugClass.title: Automatic launch starts future-due tasks
bugClass.cause: An automatic launch, claim, reservation, recovery, resumption, or final startup path can proceed without enforcing the task’s due-time eligibility check, allowing work scheduled for the future to start early. Manual starts may intentionally bypass this guard.
bugClass.criteria: Include a site if any unattended path can request, claim, reserve, recover, resume, or finally start scheduled work without checking that its due time has arrived. Each path is independently sufficient. Exclude cases where the due check is enforced before automatic dispatch and only explicit manual starts bypass it.

candidates.evidence: `trackerDispatchQueue` (lines 72–82) checks permission and then calls `dispatcher.claim`; this excerpt does not show whether due-time eligibility is enforced by `permitIntent`, the dispatcher, or an earlier automatic dispatch guard, so an unchecked automatic claim path is not established.

`serveQueue` (lines 180–192) sends non-explicit candidates through `queue.claim` and queued runs through `queue.retry`, but the excerpt does not show whether those calls enforce due-time eligibility or whether candidates were already filtered by a due guard.

Lines 59–79 enqueue wake work directly, and for queued jobs call `claim(work)` before `jobs.start(request, signal)`; claimed jobs are observed. The excerpt does not show whether due-time eligibility is enforced earlier in dispatch or whether the queued job path is automatic, so the missing guard is not established.

`unclaimedRequests` (lines 177–181) selects automatic or urgent adapter-owned items with a non-null `due`, but the excerpt ends within the SQL and does not reveal whether `now` is used to filter future due times before requests are claimed or started.
